title: Normalized coefficient fibers give a vanishing error tower
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $O$, and a scheme $T$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $B_n=(O/\ell^n)_T$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Let $Q_n$ be K-flat complexes of $B_n$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex] with strict semilinear chain transitions $q_{n,m}:Q_n\to Q_m$ for $1\leq m\leq n$, satisfying identities and the cocycle law. Assume every actual reduction map $Q_n\otimes_{B_n}B_m\to Q_m$, $x\otimes b\mapsto bq_{n,m}(x)$, is a quasi-isomorphism. No boundedness or constructibility is assumed.

Fix $m\geq1$ and, for $n\geq m$, put $K_m=[R\xrightarrow{\ell^m}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$, $P_{n,m}=B_n\otimes_RK_m$, $F_{n,m}=\operatorname{Cone}(P_{n,m}\to B_m)[-1]$, and $S_n=Q_n\otimes_{B_n}B_m$, using the coefficient augmentation and total tensor convention of [lem-sp-ell-coefficient-fiber, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. There is a distinguished triangle of strict $R$-towers on $n\geq m$ whose terms are $Q_n\otimes_{B_n}F_{n,m}$, $Q_n\otimes_RK_m$, and $S_n$. Its right arrow is the coefficient augmentation, with the middle identification induced by $x\otimes(b\otimes k)\mapsto bx\otimes k$. The left tower is quasi-isomorphic to the tower $S_n[1]$ with transition from $n'$ to $n$ equal to $\ell^{n'-n}$ times the usual transition on $S$. The maps $S_n\to Q_m$ above form a strict levelwise quasi-isomorphism to the constant tower on $Q_m$.

For total derived inverse limits of strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], the left tower has zero limit and the composite
$$R\!\lim_{n\geq m}(Q_n\otimes_RK_m)\longrightarrow R\!\lim_{n\geq m}S_n\longrightarrow Q_m$$
is an isomorphism in $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The last arrow is induced by the displayed strict map to the constant tower, using its diagonal identification with $Q_m$. Thus this composite is the one induced by the original transition maps and coefficient augmentations.

proof.text: Write $A_n=Q_n\otimes_{B_n}F_{n,m}$ and $M_n=Q_n\otimes_RK_m$. The coefficient maps of [lem-sp-ell-coefficient-fiber] and the given semilinear $q_{n',n}$ define the strict transitions on $A$, $M$ and $S$: on tensors they are $x\otimes f\mapsto q_{n',n}(x)\otimes\bar f$, $x\otimes k\mapsto q_{n',n}(x)\otimes k$, and $x\otimes b\mapsto q_{n',n}(x)\otimes b$, respectively. Semilinearity makes these balanced; identities and cocycles follow on these generators, hence on sheaf tensor products. The mutually inverse balanced maps $x\otimes(b\otimes k)\mapsto bx\otimes k$ and $x\otimes k\mapsto x\otimes(1\otimes k)$ identify $Q_n\otimes_{B_n}P_{n,m}$ with $M_n$. Since $b$ has degree zero, the total differentials agree without an extra sign [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Both maps commute with transitions, and the tensored coefficient augmentation becomes $a_n:M_n\to S_n$, $x\otimes k\mapsto x\otimes\epsilon_m(k)$.

source.place: Proof paragraph: coefficient-fiber triangles, normalization and vanishing left term.

proof.text: The rotated cone triangle of $\epsilon_{n,m}:P_{n,m}\to B_m$ is $F_{n,m}\to P_{n,m}\to B_m\to F_{n,m}[1]$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-triangulated-category]. Apply the tensor-cone and shift comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs] with fixed first factor $Q_n$. They identify its tensor image with the rotated cone triangle of $a_n$, giving $A_n\to M_n\xrightarrow{a_n}S_n\to A_n[1]$. More explicitly the comparison on a $Q_n^p$ times cone-target summand is identity, and on a $Q_n^p$ times cone-source summand it is multiplication by $(-1)^p$. These formulas preserve the augmentation and connecting arrow. Every transition has degree zero, respects scalar multiplication and commutes with $\epsilon$; thus the same summand formulas commute with the semilinear transitions, although the rings $B_n$ vary. Consequently the comparisons form chain isomorphisms of strict $R$-towers to the rotated cone triangle of the strict chain map $a:M\to S$. This proves distinguishedness in the derived category of strict towers, using its levelwise abelian structure [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian].

source.place: Proof paragraph: coefficient-fiber triangles, normalization and vanishing left term.

proof.text:
Let $\eta_n:B_m[1]\to F_{n,m}$ be the quasi-isomorphism in [lem-sp-ell-coefficient-fiber]. Since $Q_n$ is K-flat, [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs] says that $1\otimes\eta_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism without a boundedness assumption. Identify $Q_n\otimes_{B_n}B_m[1]$ with $S_n[1]$ by sending $x\otimes b$ for $x\in Q_n^p$ to $(-1)^p x\otimes b$ in the shifted total complex. Indeed the differential on $S_n[1]$ is $-d_{S_n}$, so this sign makes the identification a chain map. Put $E_n=S_n[1]$ with transition $e_{n',n}=\ell^{n'-n}s_{n',n}[1]$, where $s$ is the usual transition on $S$. The coefficient identity $f_{n',n}\eta_{n'}=\eta_n\ell^{n'-n}$ gives
$$a^A_{n',n}(1\otimes\eta_{n'})=(1\otimes\eta_n)(\ell^{n'-n}s_{n',n}[1]),$$
after the signed shift identifications; the signs agree because $q_{n',n}$ preserves $p$. Thus these maps give a strict levelwise quasi-isomorphism $E\to A$. Evaluation is exact [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so kernels, images and cohomology are levelwise: this map is a quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes and becomes an isomorphism in their derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Proof paragraph: coefficient-fiber triangles, normalization and vanishing left term.

proof.text:
Define $\rho_n:S_n\to Q_m$ by $\rho_n(x\otimes b)=bq_{n,m}(x)$. For $n'\geq n\geq m$, the cocycle law gives
$$\rho_n s_{n',n}(x\otimes b)=bq_{n,m}q_{n',n}(x)=bq_{n',m}(x)=\rho_{n'}(x\otimes b).$$
Hence $\rho:S\to\Delta Q_m$ is a strict tower map. Its components are precisely the quasi-isomorphisms assumed in the statement; at $n=m$ it is the canonical unit $Q_m\otimes_{B_m}B_m\cong Q_m$. Exact evaluation [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] makes $\rho$ a quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes, so its image in the localized derived tower category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is an isomorphism. Applying the functor $R\lim$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] gives an isomorphism $R\lim S\to R\lim\Delta Q_m$.

source.place: Proof paragraph: coefficient-fiber triangles, normalization and vanishing left term.

proof.text: Every term of $S_n$ is a $B_m$-module, so $\ell^mS_n=0$ as a complex. Therefore $e_{n+m,n}=\ell^m s_{n+m,n}[1]=0$ as a chain map. The strict quasi-isomorphism $E\to A$ of step 3 gives, at these two levels, $a^A_{n+m,n}=\eta^Q_n e_{n+m,n}(\eta^Q_{n+m})^{-1}=0$ in $D(R)$. The site is the small pro-etale site fixed by [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]; $R$ is a commutative ring sheaf. Reindexing $n\geq m$ by $n=m+j-1$ puts these towers exactly under [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Its pro-zero conclusion applies to $A$ and gives $R\lim A=0$. This uses a fixed gap $m$, with no cohomological bounds and no assertion about exactness of ordinary products.

source.place: Proof paragraph: coefficient-fiber triangles, normalization and vanishing left term.

proof.text: We check the specified diagonal identification for the constant tower. Choose a K-injective resolution $i:Q_m\to I$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the small ringed site of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. For any complex of towers $Z$, a chain map $Z\to\Delta I$ is determined by its component $Z_m\to I$: the component at $n\geq m$ is its composite with $Z_n\to Z_m$. The same statement holds for homotopies. If $Z$ is acyclic, $Z_m$ is acyclic by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; K-injectivity of $I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] therefore makes every $Z\to\Delta I$ null-homotopic. Thus $\Delta I$ is K-injective, and $\Delta i$ is a levelwise quasi-isomorphism. The resolution formula in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] computes $R\lim\Delta Q_m$ by $\lim\Delta I=I$, with each projection the identity of $I$. The diagonal $d:Q_m\to R\lim\Delta Q_m$ induced by the identity cone is represented by $i$, hence is invertible. Its inverse is exactly the diagonal identification used in the statement. This is a direct adjunction calculation, not an appeal to termwise products computing unbounded derived products.

source.place: Tag 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives), direct adjunction calculation; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), K-injective computation; injectives.tex Tag 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck).

proof.text: Exactness of $R\lim$ in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] sends the strict cone triangle in step 2 to a distinguished triangle $0\to R\lim M\xrightarrow{u}R\lim S\to0$, where $u=R\lim(a)$. To check that this actual arrow is invertible, apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] and rotations from [def-weil-triangulated-category]. With $B=R\lim S$ exactness gives $r:B\to R\lim M$ such that $ur=1_B$. With $W=R\lim M$ the backwards rotated triangle shows that composition with $u$ is injective, since its preceding term is zero; hence $ru=1$. Thus $u$ is invertible. Step 4 gives the invertible $R\lim(\rho)$, and step 6 gives the invertible $d^{-1}$. Their composite $d^{-1}R\lim(\rho)R\lim(a)$ is therefore an isomorphism $R\lim(Q_n\otimes_RK_m)\to Q_m$. The maps $a$ and $\rho$ were the actual strict augmentation and transition-induced reduction maps, and $d$ was the identity diagonal cone. Functoriality of the total derived functor therefore identifies this composite with exactly the composite in the statement.
